title: Two Weeks, Zero Applications: How an Agent Fixed Itself | vitalii.no
description:
Between August 19 and 31, every job that landed on a platform my job-search agent hadn't learned yet just sat there. The consent button that grants recon access needed a tap within a 120-minute window, and I never made it in time. Scanning and scoring kept running fine every day, but two full weeks passed without a single application actually going out.

I changed the fill gate in scripts/patch-agent-pollers.cjs so the agent can grant itself recon access on its own, up to a daily cap of new platforms (2 by default). The grant is stamped onto the job row itself, in skyvern_metadata.auto_recon_granted, before the agent wakes up — so the daily budget is spent exactly once per row and survives the stuck-timeout watchdog. When several unlearned platforms are queued at once, the budget goes to whichever host has the most waiting jobs, since recon knowledge generalizes per host, not per job. The manual consent button and a file-based override still work as a backup.

Learning a brand-new platform costs roughly 6.8 million tokens, so capping it at a couple of hosts a day keeps that cost bounded while still clearing a backlog that used to sit idle for weeks.
